info.title: DetectifAI Developer API
info.summary: Detect AI-generated speech and verify speakers by voice.
info.description:
The DetectifAI developer API detects synthetic (AI-generated) speech and verifies speakers by voice.

**Authentication.** Send your API key in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer dtf_live_...`.
Keys are created in the dashboard and shown once. Never put keys in URLs.

**Credits.** Detection, enrollment and verification use credits from your account balance; your balance is
shown in the dashboard and at `GET /v1/credits`. Only completed checks use credits: a rejected file, a busy
service or a failed check uses none. A verification with `detect_deepfake=true` counts as two checks.

**Uploads.** Send audio as `multipart/form-data` (field `file`), up to 100 MB. The whole upload must arrive
within 120 s (at no less than 64 KB/s); larger or slower uploads are rejected (`413`, `408`). When too many
large uploads are in progress the API answers `503 server_busy` with `Retry-After`. Durations are checked
after decoding: enrollment 15-60 s with at least 10 s of speech, verification 3-60 s with at least 2 s of
speech, deepfake detection 0.5-120 s.

**Retries.** Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (for example a new UUID) with every detection, enrollment and
verification request, and send the same key again if you retry it. The retry returns the stored response
(`idempotent_replay: true`, header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) without running the check again or using
credits again. Keys are remembered for 24 h; results stay available for 30 days at
`GET /v1/operations/{operation_id}`.

**Errors.** Every non-2xx response uses the same envelope:
`{"error": {"type", "code", "message", "param"}, "request_id"}`. Every response carries `X-Request-Id`.

**Reading results.** `score` (0 to 1) says how likely a recording is AI-generated and `similarity` (-1 to 1)
how alike two voices are. Each result carries the `threshold` used for its decision. Results are strong
signals, not proof: try them on your own recordings before relying on them.

post.description: Checks whether a recording contains AI-generated speech. Send one audio file longer than 4 seconds and at most 120 seconds. Use the result's `verdict`: `real`, `fake`, or `not_sure` when the recording cannot be judged reliably (try a longer or cleaner recording); `decided_by` says which check decided it. `score` is the main model's score (0 to 1, higher means more likely AI-generated), kept for older clients together with `label` and `is_synthetic`. A `not_sure` verdict uses credits like any result, except when part of the check was unavailable (`decided_by: fallback`): then no credits are used. Main failures: the file is not audio or is damaged (415/422), 4 seconds or shorter or longer than 120 seconds (422), not enough credits (402), the service is busy (503, retry later). Requires scope `deepfake:detect`.

post.description: Saves a voice sample for a speaker so that later recordings can be verified against it. The speaker is created on first use. Send a recording of 15-60 seconds with at least 10 seconds of clear speech from that one person. Up to 5 samples per speaker; 2-3 samples from different sessions make verification more reliable. Main failures: too short, too long or too little speech (422, the message says what is needed), the speaker already has 5 samples (409), not enough credits (402). Requires scope `speakers:enroll`.

post.summary: Say whether a result was right
post.description: Tells us whether an AI-speech check (`deepfake.detect`) got it right. Send `correct`, and optionally what the recording really is (`label`: `real` or `fake`) and a short note. Only for checks of your own account; sending again replaces your earlier answer. No credits are used. We store your answer with the result, not the audio: keeping recordings for review would need your explicit consent and is not offered yet. Requires the scope of the check (`deepfake:detect`).
